title: The Stoic Week: What Is Yours to Do

source.author: Epictetus
source.rights: Public domain in the United States
source.note: Section numbers 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10 and 17 were checked against the Project Gutenberg text of this edition on 2026-11-09. Each matches the concept listed for its day.

through_line: Each day narrows the question 'what is actually mine?' and then turns it into something the learner does. Day 7 adds no new concept; it retrieves the other six.
end_of_week_artifact: The learner's seven reflections, compiled into a personal handbook they can export. 'Enchiridion' means handbook, so the week ends with the learner having written a small one of their own.

lessons.title: Two Lists
lessons.objective: Sort a real situation into what is and is not up to you.
lessons.misconception_targeted: outcome-as-control: believing effort entitles you to a result
lessons.practice: Once today, when something irritates you, ask: which list is this on?

lessons.title: The Event and the Story
lessons.concept: We are disturbed by our judgments about events, not by the events
lessons.objective: Separate what happened from the judgment you added to it.
lessons.misconception_targeted: suppression: thinking Stoicism means not having feelings
lessons.practice: Write one upsetting event as a bare fact, then write the judgment you attached to it.

lessons.title: Aim Your Wanting
lessons.concept: Desire and aversion belong only on things that are up to you
lessons.objective: Rewrite one goal so that reaching it depends only on you.
lessons.practice: Take one thing you want this week and restate it as something you do rather than something you get.

lessons.title: Rehearse the Bathhouse
lessons.concept: Anticipate what an activity involves, and carry a second goal: keeping your own conduct intact
lessons.objective: Plan for a predictable annoyance before it happens.
lessons.misconception_targeted: pessimism: confusing rehearsal with expecting the worst
lessons.practice: Before one task today, name what is likely to go wrong and what you intend to keep steady.

lessons.title: Wanting What Happens
lessons.concept: Stop demanding that events match your wishes; align your wishes with events
lessons.objective: Distinguish acceptance of an event from giving up on action.
lessons.practice: Pick one thing that has already happened and cannot be changed. Say what you will do next, given that it happened.

lessons.title: What Do You Have for This?
lessons.concept: For every difficulty, ask which capacity you already have for meeting it
lessons.objective: Match a current difficulty to a capacity you can exercise.
lessons.misconception_targeted: defensiveness: treating Stoicism as only a shield and never a way of acting
lessons.practice: Name one difficulty you are facing and the capacity it calls for: patience, restraint, endurance, or another.

lessons.title: Play the Part Well
lessons.concept: Synthesis: the role is assigned; playing it well is yours
lessons.objective: Explain the week's ideas in your own words using one situation from your own life.
lessons.misconception_targeted: fatalism: thinking an assigned role means nothing you do matters
lessons.practice: Read back your six reflections and write a seventh that begins: 'What is mine to do is...'
